stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $u:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}$ be a functor and let $u^p$ be the precomposition functor on presheaves. For $V\in\Ob(\mathcal{D})$ define the category ${}_V^u\mathcal{I}$ with objects $(U,\psi:u(U)\to V)$ and arrows $\alpha:(U,\psi)\to(U',\psi')$ satisfying $\psi=\psi'\circ u(\alpha)$. Define the presheaf ${}_pu\mathcal{F}$ for any presheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$ by
\[
({}_pu\mathcal{F})(V)=\lim_{({}_V^u\mathcal{I})^{opp}}\mathcal{F}(U),
\]
with its canonical restriction maps (source §19, L4078–4116).
The functor ${}_pu$ is a right adjoint to the functor $u^p$.
In other words the formula
$$
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(u^p\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{F})
=
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{D})}(\mathcal{G}, {}_pu\mathcal{F})
$$
holds bifunctorially in $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$.

reason: The right adjoint presheaf formula is obtained by dualizing the previously proved left-adjoint comma-category formula to Set^op-valued presheaves. The source also identifies the requisite counit explicitly; the categorical duality gives the bifunctorial Hom bijection.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ and $v : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$
be functors of categories. Assume that $v$ is right adjoint to $u$.
Then we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item $u^ph_V = h_{v(V)}$ for any $V$ in $\mathcal{D}$,
\item the category $\mathcal{I}^v_U$ has an initial object,
\item the category ${}_V^u\mathcal{I}$ has a final object,
\item ${}_pu = v^p$, and
\item $u^p = v_p$.
\end{enumerate}

reason: The adjunction u⊣v identifies representables under precomposition, supplies an initial object in the relevant left comma category and a final object in its dual. Yoneda plus the presheaf adjunction then gives _pu=v^p, and uniqueness of adjoints yields u^p=v_p.
